items.title: Section: Skill in Treatises Closes — Beyond Learning and Reflection Alone, Into a Pure Faith Actually Earned Through Realisation

items.zh: 又為了知所餘新新後後法義殊勝差別，雖復聞思已到究竟，而由此故漸次成熟，於此法義獲得淨信。由是行相，當知菩薩知諸論智無量圓滿、無有顛倒。
items.en: Furthermore, in order to know the further, ever-newer, progressively more excellent distinctions of meaning still remaining, bodhisattvas, even once learning and reflection have already reached their own completion, continue on this basis to mature gradually still further, and thereby obtain a genuinely pure faith regarding this teaching and its meaning. Through this manner of practice, one should understand that a bodhisattva's wisdom of skill in treatises becomes boundless, complete, and entirely free of distortion.

items.title: Section: Skill in Worldly Knowledge Opens — the Sentient World's Own Perilous, Benighted Nature, Dying and Being Born Again Without Ever Learning the Way Up or Out

items.zh: 云何菩薩善知世間？謂諸菩薩，普於一切有情世間，如實了知如是世間極為艱嶮，甚為愚闇。所謂雖有生老及死，數數死生，而諸有情於老死等上昇、出離不如實知。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skill in worldly knowledge? Bodhisattvas who, throughout the entire world of sentient beings, correctly and thoroughly recognise that this world is extremely perilous and profoundly benighted. That is to say, although there is birth, ageing, and death, and beings die and are born again and again, they do not correctly and thoroughly know how to rise above old age and death, nor how to genuinely depart from them.

items.title: Section: The Five Turbidities — Shrinking Lifespans, Beings Who No Longer Honour Even Their Own Parents, Rampant Affliction, Counterfeit Teaching Mistaken for the Real Thing, and the Three Classical Calamities Closing an Age

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，如實了知有情世間，有諸穢濁，濁世增時；無諸穢濁，濁世減時。謂依五濁。一者、壽濁，二者、有情濁，三者、煩惱濁，四者、見濁，五者、劫濁。如於今時人壽短促，極長壽者不過百年。昔時不爾。是名壽濁。如於今時，有情多分不識父母，不識沙門、若婆羅門，不識家長可尊敬者、作義利者、作所作者，於今世罪及後世罪不見怖畏，不修惠施、不作福業、不受齋法、不受淨戒，昔時不爾。是名有情濁。如於今時，有情多分習非法貪、不平等貪，執持刀劍、執持器仗，鬪訟諍競，多行諂誑詐偽妄語，攝受邪法，有無量種惡不善法現可了知，昔時不爾。是名煩惱濁。如於今時，有情多分為壞正法、為滅正法，造立眾多像似正法，虛妄推求邪法邪義以為先故。昔時不爾。是名見濁。如於今時，漸次趣入饑饉中劫，現有眾多饑饉可得；漸次趣入疫病中劫，現有眾多疫病可得；漸次趣入刀兵中劫，現有眾多互相殘害刀兵可得；昔時不爾。是名劫濁。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly recognise that the world of sentient beings has various defiling turbidities during a period of increasing degeneration, and lacks these various defiling turbidities during a period of decreasing degeneration. This concerns five turbidities: first, the turbidity of lifespan; second, the turbidity of beings; third, the turbidity of affliction; fourth, the turbidity of view; fifth, the turbidity of the eon. Just as, in the present age, human lifespan is short and pressing, the very longest-lived reaching no more than a hundred years, whereas it was not so in earlier times — this is called the turbidity of lifespan. Just as, in the present age, beings for the most part no longer recognise their own parents, nor renunciants, nor brahmins, and see no cause for dread in either present or future wrongdoing, no longer practising generosity, cultivating merit, observing fasting precepts, or receiving pure discipline, whereas it was not so in earlier times — this is called the turbidity of beings. Just as, in the present age, beings for the most part habitually indulge in unlawful craving and inequitable craving, take up swords and weapons, engage in disputes and litigation, and commit much flattering, deceitful, and false speech, embracing wrong teachings — this is called the turbidity of affliction. Just as, in the present age, beings for the most part work to corrupt and destroy the true teaching, fabricating a great many counterfeit teachings resembling the true dharma, falsely and deceptively pursuing wrong teachings and wrong meanings as though they came first — this is called the turbidity of view. Just as, in the present age, the world gradually enters an intermediate eon of famine, then gradually enters an intermediate eon of plague, then gradually enters an intermediate eon of warfare — this is called the turbidity of the eon.

items.zh: 是名菩薩如實了知有情世間。

items.title: Section: The Container World's Own Rise and Fall — Fire Reaching the First Absorption, Water Reaching the Second, Wind Reaching the Third, and a Cosmos Rebuilt From the Very Top Down

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，如實了知諸器世間破壞成立，如器世間破壞成立差別而知。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly recognise the container world's own destruction and formation, knowing it exactly according to the distinct pattern of the container world's own destruction and formation.

items.title: Section: Eight Ways of Observing the World — the Four Noble Truths Doubled Through the World's Own Arising, Its Cessation, and the Paths That Actually Lead There

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於其世間，於世間集，於世間滅，於能往趣世間集行，於能往趣世間滅行，於其世間愛味、過患及與出離皆如實知。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly know the world itself; the world's own arising; the world's own cessation; the path leading towards the world's arising; the path leading towards the world's cessation; and the world's own alluring taste, its actual dangers, and genuine release from it.

items.title: Section: Worldly Ultimate Truth — a Person Is Only Five Aggregates in Flux, and Every Word Ever Spoken About One Is Mere Convention

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，如實了知眼乃至意諸無色蘊，四大造色，成士夫身，唯有爾所假名人性。於中所有想，或我、或有情，此唯有想。於中所有自號言說，我眼見色，廣說乃至我意知法，此亦唯有自號言說。於中所有世俗語言，謂此長老有如是名、如是種類、如是族姓、如是飲食、如是領納若苦若樂、如是長壽、如是久住、如是盡其壽量邊際，此亦唯有世俗言說。菩薩於此皆如實知。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly recognise that the formless aggregates from the eye consciousness through to the mind consciousness, together with form built from the four great elements, together constitute what is called a human body — this much, and no more, is what the provisional label "person" actually refers to. Whatever notion of "I" or "a sentient being" arises regarding this — this is nothing but a mere notion. Whatever self-referential speech arises regarding this, such as "I see form with my eye," and so on up through "I know phenomena with my mind" — this too is nothing but mere self-referential speech. Whatever worldly language arises regarding this, such as "this elder has such a name, such a caste, such a family lineage, such a diet, receives such pleasant or painful experience, has such a long life, has dwelt so long already, and will exhaust the full span of such a lifetime" — this too is nothing but mere worldly convention. Bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly know all of this exactly as it is.

items.zh: 由諸菩薩如實了知有情世間流轉差別、若器世間流轉差別、若八種相觀世間義、若諸世間所有勝義，是故說名善知世間。

items.title: Section: Putting Worldly Knowledge Into Practice — Freedom From Pride Towards the More Accomplished, the Equal, and, Most Delicately, the Dew-Fragile Resolve of the Less Accomplished

items.zh: 復次，菩薩若見年德俱尊勝者，能正奉迎，敷座延坐，敬問、禮拜、合掌、慇勤，修和敬業。若見年德俱相似者，能正問訊、酬對、歡慰，以軟美言共興談論，不依等慢而自格量。若見年德俱卑劣者，隨力隨能勸修勝德；顯實少德，覆實多過，終不舉發令其恥愧；亦不輕陵令心退沒；知有希求若財若法，終不背面，亦不顰蹙；不譏誤失，不蔑退榮。
items.en: Furthermore, when bodhisattvas see someone of greater age and virtue, they properly welcome them, prepare a seat and invite them to sit, and treat them with respectful inquiry, prostration, joined palms, and earnest attention, cultivating the conduct of harmonious respect. When they see someone of equal age and virtue, they properly greet them, converse and rejoice together, discussing matters with gentle, agreeable speech, never secretly measuring themselves against the other through the conceit of equality. When they see someone of lesser age and virtue, they encourage, according to their own strength and ability, the cultivation of excellent qualities; they bring out whatever little genuine virtue is actually present while covering over whatever many genuine faults exist, never exposing them so as to cause shame, and never belittling them so as to cause their resolve to falter. Knowing that such a person hopes for either wealth or the teaching, bodhisattvas never turn away or frown; they neither mock the person's mistakes nor disdain their diminished standing.

items.title: Section: Receiving Beings With Wealth and Teaching, Never With a Trace of Arrogance However Exalted One's Own Standing

items.zh: 於是一切劣等勝品諸有情類，若見彼時，先意慰問，讚言善來，無倒安處，能正隨力攝以財法。雖處尊勝，而於有情終不乖戾，不自珍奇，亦不憍傲。
items.en: Towards all these beings, whether of lesser, equal, or greater standing, when bodhisattvas encounter them, they first offer a comforting word, praising their arrival as welcome, correctly settling them without distortion, and correctly gathering them in with wealth or with the teaching according to their own strength. Although occupying an exalted, superior standing, bodhisattvas are never, towards any being, harsh or discordant, never treat themselves as uniquely precious, and are never arrogant.

blocks.text: The bodhisattva's knowledge of the world: its beings, its ages, its physical cycles, and how to behave within it.
Beyond hearing and reflection, the bodhisattva studies further to know "ever-newer distinctions of meaning", until faith rests on realisation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the four kinds of realised faith.

"Extremely perilous and profoundly benighted", beings dying and reborn "without learning the way up or out". Master Cháng Bǎi: humans and gods escaping the lower realms is "rising"; the three vehicles, "going out".

Of lifespan, of beings (who no longer honour their parents), of affliction, of views (counterfeit teaching mistaken for the real), of the age. Master Cháng Bǎi explains increasing and decreasing aeons.

Its destruction and formation: fire reaching the first absorption heaven, water the second, wind the third, "a cosmos rebuilt from the top down". Master Cháng Bǎi explains the order of the three great calamities.

subs.head: Eight ways of knowing the world

blocks.text: The world, its arising, cessation, the path to each, and its taste, danger, and escape.
"A person is only five aggregates in flux; every word about one is convention." Master Cháng Bǎi: fifty years counts as "long life", eighty "dwelt long".

Towards elders: welcome, a seat, respect. Towards equals and juniors: "bringing out whatever little virtue is present while covering many faults". Venerable Miào Jìng: don't think "Am I any worse than you?" Towards all: "first offering a comforting word, praising their arrival". Master Cháng Bǎi: say "svāgata", "welcome".

quiz.q: "Skill in treatises" means a bodhisattva has properly received and mastered what?
options: the five branches of learning expressed through names, phrases, syllables
quiz.why: "Every teaching belonging to the five branches of classical learning, expressed through name, phrase, and syllable." Master Cháng Bǎi: inner science, logic, medicine, linguistics, and the crafts. Venerable Miào Jìng: syllables form names, names form phrases, and that becomes a book.

quiz.q: "Even once learning and reflection are complete … obtaining pure faith." How do the lectures view this faith?
options: Cháng Bǎi: this is cultivated wisdom — faith from real practice and realisation; Miào Jìng: this "realised purity" means attaining the noble path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this refers to cultivated wisdom — the faith comes from real practice and realisation, the four kinds of realised purity belonging to stream-enterers and above. Venerable Miào Jìng: this realised purity means attaining the noble path.

quiz.q: "Not knowing how to rise above or depart from ageing and death." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish "rising" and "departing"?
options: ordinary humans and gods leaving the three lower realms is rising; the three vehicles' liberation from the three realms is departing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary humans and gods escaping the three lower realms is "rising"; the three vehicles and bodhisattvas being liberated from the three realms is "departing." Venerable Miào Jìng: transcending the nine grounds of the three realms.

quiz.q: What are the five turbidities named in the treatise?
quiz.why: "Five turbidities: of lifespan, of beings, of affliction, of view, of the eon." Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodily and verbal deeds of the sentient world are "defilement," mental deeds "turbidity."

quiz.q: The treatise just says bodhisattvas know the container world's destruction and formation. How do the lectures fill this in?
options: Miào Jìng: this is the great three calamities; Cháng Bǎi: fire reaches the first absorption, water the second, wind the third, and formation starts from the third
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this explains the great three calamities. Master Cháng Bǎi: fire comes first, once per great eon, burning up to the first absorption heaven; water reaches the second, wind the third; formation begins from the third absorption heaven — last destroyed, first formed.

quiz.q: In worldly language — "such a long life, dwelt so long, the full span of lifetime" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: fifty is "long life," eighty "dwelt long," over a hundred the "full span"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: fifty counts as "long life," eighty as "dwelt long," over a hundred as "the full span" — eight kinds of conventional expression applied to a living being.

quiz.q: Seeing someone of lesser age and virtue, how does the bodhisattva treat them?
options: bring out their little virtue, cover their many faults, never expose or belittle them
quiz.why: "Bringing out whatever little genuine virtue is present while covering over many faults, never exposing them so as to cause shame, never belittling them so their resolve falters." Master Cháng Bǎi: otherwise their dew-like resolve quickly evaporates.
